title: Quantitative homogenization for the critical long-range random conductance model
summary: We consider the long-range random conductance model on $\mathbb{Z}^d$ at the critical exponent: the jump rate between sites $x$ and $y$ decays as $\mathbf{a}(x,y) |x-y|^{-(d+2)}$, where $\mathbf{a}(x,y)$ are i.i.d. uniformly elliptic conductances. Below the critical exponent $(d+2)$ the walk converges to a stable process; above it, to Brownian motion with diffusive $\sqrt{t}$ scaling.
